decisive_items: exploratory laparotomy “showed no mechanical cause of the obstructions”
CT scan showed small-bowel dilation (approximately 23 mm in diameter) consistent with obstruction
recurrent episodes of abdominal pain, bloating, and obstipation
response.rationale: Chronic recurrent obstructive symptoms without mechanical cause, plus bowel dilation and megacolon, strongly indicate a motility disorder. R6 adds the 'chronic' qualifier matching the 20-year history, while R5 is the same entity without that specificity.

rejected.why: No bowel resection or short bowel anatomy; dilation and megacolon are not features of short bowel syndrome.
Endoscopy showed no celiac disease and gluten-free diet failed, directly contradicting this diagnosis.
No evidence of protein-losing enteropathy or lymphatic abnormalities; obstructive pattern and megacolon are not typical.
Alcohol use is present but symptoms began after cholecystectomy and no liver failure signs; the obstructive pattern is not explained by liver disease.
